To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) Cd fluxes from soil to plant and plant to snail are the most sensitive parameters for assessing Cd transfer to snail in the field, 2) snail Cd concentrations are not affected by the soil pH, 3) the seasonal variations in snail Cd concentrations can be explained by the variations in the snail mass.
Cd accumulation in the snail Helix aspersa was found to be dependent on the soil Cd content, the snail mass and the season, but was not influenced by soil pH.
the transfer of cadmium from soils to terrestrial snails is a time-integrated function of soil Cd concentration and snail growth.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development and application of new tools for the improvement of the environmental risk assessment of metals.
the development of a new approach to the study of the transfer of toxic elements from soil to snails, based on the use of toxicokinetics.
the study of the transfer of Cd in the soil-snail food chain.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

snails can be used as bioindicators of Cd pollution in soils, and that the use of toxicokinetic parameters is a useful tool to quantify the transfer and to improve the reliability of the assessment of the environmental quality.

the present study provides a useful tool for the evaluation of the environmental risk of Cd contamination in soils and for a better understanding of the factors controlling metal bioavailability and bioaccumulation.
the use of snails as bioindicators of soil contamination is possible and reliable.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the snail is a good candidate for the assessment of the Cd transfer in a soil- plant- animal system.
Cd transfer to terrestrial snail species is a sensitive tool for the detection of Cd contamination of the soil.
the use of snails in environmental biomonitorning is a good way to assess Cd bioavailability and transfer from soil to organisms.
The main takeaway from our work is that
toxicokinetics is an interesting tool in improving the risk assessment procedures and quantifying metal bioavailability in a defined target.
toxicokinetics can be used to improve the risk assessment procedures and to quantify metal bioaccumulation in a more accurate and sensitive way.
the toxicokinetics approach, which is based on the measurement of metal fluxes in organisms, is a promising tool in environmental biomonitorings.
